summary: Briery Knob tower in Pocahontas County was dismantled; FFLOS says portions went to the Nettie Volunteer Fire Department, where a 2013 conference record places a tower.

facts.status_note: FFLOS says the tower was dismantled and portions went to the Nettie Volunteer Fire Department. The original summit is listed as gone.

staffing.status: watchman at night during high fire danger

events.note: Lumber company built more than 25 miles of telephone line to reach the Briery Knob station (1913-14 report)
Watchman S.A. Sparks; station supervised from the Little Levels district
Tower had telephone connections with two companies
Forest supervisor said the road to the tower would be improved for tourists; completion not confirmed
Eastern conference minutes describe a Briery Knob tower sitting behind the Nettie FD; move date still unknown

evidence.supports: Location within the Monongahela National Forest, Pocahontas County

evidence.quote: 1914 photo from WV Fish & Game Commission report

evidence.supports: A lumber company built over 25 miles of telephone line to reach the station in 1913-14
evidence.quote: The Cherry River Boom and Lumber Company constructed at their own expense more than twenty-five miles of telephone lines in order to make connection with Briery Knob and Job Knob Stations.

evidence.supports: In 1916 a watchman stayed at the station only at night in high fire danger
evidence.quote: The watchman, S.A. Sparks, lives at Lobelia, three miles distant, and only stays at the station at night when there is great danger from fire.

evidence.supports: The station was under supervision from the Little Levels district
evidence.quote: This station is located in Little Levels District, Pocahontas County, twelve miles from Seebert, and is under supervision of David Frame.
The Briery Knob tower in Pocahontas County has connection with the Cloverlick and Durbin Telephone Company and the Marlinton and Elk Telephone Company.

evidence.supports: 1938 statement by the forest supervisor that the road would be improved so tourists could enjoy the view
evidence.quote: the road to Briery Knob fire tower in Pocahontas county would be improved so that tourists 'may enjoy the view from the peak.'

evidence.supports: Tower dismantled; portions relocated to the Nettie Volunteer Fire Department
evidence.quote: This tower was dismantled. Portions were relocated to the Nettie Volunteer Fire Department.

evidence.supports: A standing tower at Nettie FD coded as relocated from Briery Knob
The original Briery Knob site is listed as gone
evidence.quote: Briery Knob Pocahontas 38.14434 -80.34444 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1647, WV 38

evidence.supports: The FFLOS register date for this entry
The Eastern lookouts page lists the West Virginia Division of Forestry as agency
The 2013 Eastern conference minutes place a Briery Knob tower behind the Nettie fire department
evidence.quote: Briery Knob tower sits behind the Netti FD in the middle of town.

corrections.current: The lookout was moved to Nettie FD.
corrections.proposed: Dismantled; portions relocated to Nettie Volunteer Fire Department
corrections.why: FFLOS says only portions were relocated. The 'moved' wording overstates it.
The 1916 report gives 4,534 feet, about 1,382 m. The brief value may come from another survey, so check before changing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says portions went to the Nettie Volunteer Fire Department. firelookout.org lists a standing tower there coded as relocated from Briery Knob. The 2013 Eastern conference minutes describe a Briery Knob tower behind the Netti FD. None of these dates the move.

notes_for_editor: No build year, designer or original station history found. The Nettie relocation rests on the FFLOS and firelookout.org entries, which share a register, plus a 2013 conference minutes note placing a Briery Knob tower behind the Nettie FD. No source dates the move. Access at Nettie and at the original summit is undocumented, so no access fact is recorded. The brief elevation (1376.8 m) differs from the 1916 figure (4,534 ft, about 1,382 m); see corrections. The FFLOS page has a 1914 photo but no image URL was captured, so none is added.
